chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, who said:

I said to Abu Al-Hasan Al-Reza (peace be upon him), 'May I be sacrificed for you! Write for me to Ismail ibn Dawud the scribe, so that I may attain (some work) from him.' He (peace be upon him) said, 'I resent for you that you should seek from the likes of this one and his like, but you can count upon my wealth.'

key_terms.أَضَنُّ بِكَ: I resent for you / I dislike for you

ai.seo_question: What did Imam Al-Reza advise regarding seeking employment or favor from others?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam Al-Reza (AS) advises the narrator to rely on the Imam's personal wealth rather than seeking patronage (*wasta*) from scribes or officials, emphasizing spiritual and material independence from the general populace. This reflects the Shia concept of the Imam as a provider who sustains his followers, reducing their need to depend on worldly power structures for livelihood. The advice underscores the virtue of dignity and self-sufficiency (*Ghina*) through divine connection rather than social climbing.

en.hubeali: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Khalid, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Abu Nasr who said,

‘I said to Abu Al-Hassan Al-Reza<sup>asws</sup>, ‘May I be sacrificed for you<sup>asws</sup>! (Please) write (a letter) for me to Ismail Bin Dawood, the scribe, so that I can attain (some work) from him’. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘I<sup>asws</sup> resent for you that you should be seeking (from) the likes of this one and his like, but you can count upon my<sup>asws</sup> wealth’.
en.sarwar: 5. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn abu Nasr who has said the following:

“Once I said to abu al-Hassan al-Rida (a.s.) ‘May Allah keep my soul in service for your cause, please write for me to Isma’il ibn Dawud al-Katib. 1 hope I will receive something from him.’ The Imam said, ‘I resent that you ask from him or similar persons. Allow it (financial help) to be paid from my property.’”
